doc.title: Ada Rovatti interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 13, 2022

title: Culture shock at Berklee and starting late
summary: Coming from a small Italian town, she found Berklee exciting and humbling, with younger students far ahead.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: Was there a bit of academic and culture shock when you went to Boston and Berklee?

Yes but I was craving for that. You know I’m coming from a small town in the north of Italy and you know when I started really playing and I started kind of really kind of loved the environment, I had a million ideas, it was hard to find somebody who was as committed as I was to music. You know the people that want to play or want to play jazz was even smaller. I was lucky there was a little big band but you know there were people that had another job and you know I wanted to practice, play new things every day, and © Fillius Jazz Archive -4-

you know it was lucky if you find somebody once every ten days. So going in an environment where everybody is so driven like I was it was exciting, refreshing and a little overwhelming also because you know the moment I stepped into Berklee I realized how poor a musician I was you know. I was just — man — especially in the summer there were kids that were high school kids that were 14, 15, and they have everything together. They had the tone, the timing, the knowledge. And I was much older than them, I was already 19, 20 because that’s when I finished high school I went to Berklee. And I didn’t have any of those things. So unfortunately it’s one thing that I still paid the toll I think that I didn’t have that background of having school, somebody to teach me when I was younger. And I always say when I do master classes at school is that you don’t realize how lucky you are. In elementary school you have the chance to pick up instruments. I saw the first saxophone when I was 16 or 17 you know. So you just sat there, and the way you learn when you are younger is much different than when you are already grown up. You know you just absorb in a different way. And I still feel that some basic of my musical puzzle are missing, some of the basics. Because I was already kind of rushing into working, I was already kind of in and out of it. So you know you don’t spend, you don’t have the freedom of like oh I can practice all day long somebody’s going to pay my bills you know. When I started to kind of —
